title: Enable Metrics Server and Explore kubectl top
description: Install the Metrics Server and use kubectl top to check node and Pod resource usage.
problemStatement:
## 🎯 Goal
Ensure the Metrics Server is running in your cluster and become familiar with `kubectl top`.

### Steps
1. Enable Metrics Server (if minikube: `minikube addons enable metrics-server`).
   For other clusters, apply the official YAML:
   ```bash
   kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/releases/latest/download/components.yaml
   ```
2. Wait for Metrics Server to be ready: `kubectl get deployment metrics-server -n kube-system`.
3. Check node metrics: `kubectl top nodes`.
4. Check Pod metrics in all namespaces: `kubectl top pods -A`.
5. Identify the Pod consuming the most memory.
6. Launch a temporary busybox that generates some CPU load:
   ```bash
   kubectl run stress --image=alpine --command -- sh -c "while true; do :; done"
   ```
7. Watch its CPU usage: `kubectl top pod stress`.
8. Delete the stress Pod.

### Questions
- Why does `kubectl top pods` show `<unknown>` for some Pods? (e.g., if Metrics Server just started)
- What does the `m` unit mean in CPU output?
hints: It may take a minute for metrics to appear after installing Metrics Server.
If `kubectl top` returns an error, check if the Metrics Server pods are running (`kubectl get pods -n kube-system | grep metrics`).
The `alpine` image might need `--restart=Never` to create a plain Pod.
expectedOutput: Node and Pod CPU/memory displayed; the stress Pod shows elevated CPU usage.
solutionCode:
# Install (if needed)
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/metrics-server/releases/latest/download/components.yaml
# Check
kubectl top nodes
kubectl top pods -A
# Create load
kubectl run stress --image=alpine --restart=Never --command -- sh -c "while true; do :; done"
kubectl top pod stress
kubectl delete pod stress
